title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). G is a profinite group generated by ρ, σ with ρ^6 = σ^4 = 1 and ρ^3 = σ^2 =: -1 (central). This makes G a quotient of SL(2,Ẑ), the profinite completion of Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 ≅ SL(2,Z), as the margin of the previous page notes. The case ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1 gives quotients of PSL(2,Ẑ). The set-up is as follows:
- τ is an involutive automorphism with τ(σ) = σ^{-1} = -σ and τ(ρ) = σρ^{-1}σ^{-1}. It is the analogue of complex conjugation, i.e. conjugation by an element of GL_2 of determinant -1.
- G' = {1,τ}·G is the semidirect product.
- ε_0 = σρ is the cusp (unipotent / parabolic) generator.
- B_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(G) × Ẑ^* is the subgroup of pairs (u,μ) with u(ε_0) = ε_0^μ, u(σ) ~ σ^μ and u(ρ) ~ ρ^μ (conjugacy in G).
B_{ρ,σ} is the analogue, for the orbifold M_{1,1} (elliptic points of orders 4 and 6, one cusp), of the 'Galois-type' automorphism groups (GT-like) that Grothendieck studies for genus 0. Its conditions are what the branch-cycle argument predicts for the Galois action on π_1 of a modular-type curve. The cusp inertia acts through the cyclotomic character μ, and the elliptic inertia generators go to conjugates of their μ-th powers.

This page simplifies the conjugacy conditions.
- Since ρ^6 = 1, ρ^μ depends only on μ mod 6, and (Z/6)^* ≅ (Z/3)^* ≅ ±1. Writing ε_3(μ) = ±1 gives (8) ρ^μ = ρ^{ε_3(μ)}.
- If ε_3(μ) = 1, u(ρ) is G-conjugate to ρ. If ε_3(μ) = -1, it is G-conjugate to ρ^{-1}.
- Equivalently, u(ρ) is conjugate to ρ by an element of G' of the form α (α ∈ G) or τα. This works because τ(ρ) = ^σ(ρ^{-1}), so ρ^{-1} is G'-conjugate to ρ through the τ-coset.
- Similarly σ has order 4, so (9) σ^μ = σ^{ε_2(μ)}, where ε_2(μ) = ±1 according to μ mod 4. Since σ^{-1} = -σ, σ^μ = ε_2(μ)σ.
- Together, ε_2 and ε_3 are the two factors of (Z/12)^* ≅ (Z/4)^* × (Z/3)^*.
- A crossed-out attempt wrote u(ρ) = ^ξρ and u(σ) = ^ησ, then ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}. It resurfaces on the next page as the cocycle-type parametrisation (13)-(14).

Proposition (completed on the next page). (u,μ) ∈ Aut(G) × Ẑ^* lies in B_{ρ,σ} if and only if there exist α in the coset G^{ε_3(μ)} of G' (i.e. α ∈ G if ε_3 = 1, α ∈ τG if ε_3 = -1) and β ∈ G such that:
- u(ρ) = int(α)(ρ),
- u(σ) = ε_2(μ)·int(β)(σ),
- u(ε_0) = ε_0^μ.

The next page goes on to parametrise (u,μ) by (α, β, ε_2(μ)). It also notes that μ is determined by u when n ↦ ε_0^n is injective. The purpose is to describe a GT-type group for arbitrary (profinite) quotients of the modular group SL(2,Ẑ), the genus-1 / M_{1,1} part of the 'équation des lacets' program.
errors: No mathematical error. The reduction ρ^μ = ρ^{ε_3(μ)} is correct because (Z/6)^* = {±1}. σ^μ = σ^{ε_2(μ)} = ε_2(μ)σ is correct because σ^{-1} = σ^3 = σ^2σ = -σ.

The equivalence with conjugation by the τ-coset is correct but stated loosely. It uses ρ^{-1} = int(σ^{-1}τ)(ρ), so the conjugating element is gσ^{-1}τ, which lies in the τ-coset of G'. The margin of the previous page suggests normalising instead with τ' = σ^{-1}τ (or στ), which satisfies τ'(ρ) = ρ^{-1}.
In the Proposition, 'Aut(G'_{ρ,σ} × Ẑ^*)' should read Aut(G) × Ẑ^*. The subscript on G for α is ambiguous in the manuscript; the intended meaning is the coset of G' indexed by ε_3(μ).
The proposition is not finished on this page; its conditions (10)-(12) are on the next page.

ideas.what: Presentation of quotients of SL(2,Ẑ) by generators ρ (order 6) and σ (order 4) with ρ^3 = σ^2 central, plus a conjugation-type involution τ.
ideas.modern_name: Profinite completion of the amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 ≅ SL(2,Z); outer involution from GL_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Serre, Trees; standard modular group theory)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in La Longue Marche (1981) and the Esquisse (genus 1 / modular tower); unsure

ideas.what: Group B_{ρ,σ} of pairs (u,μ): u fixes the cusp generator up to the cyclotomic power and sends the elliptic generators to conjugates of their μ-th powers.
ideas.modern_name: Modular / genus-one analogue of GT; Galois-type automorphisms of π_1^orb(M_{1,1}) and its quotients (branch-cycle conditions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (GT' and SL2 relations, ~1997); Nakamura; Hain–Matsumoto; Enriquez (elliptic GT, 2014); Guillot (GT of finite groups / PSL2Z, ~2014-2018)
ideas.where_published: Theme of La Longue Marche / Esquisse (Teichmüller tower, genus 1), but this explicit definition for arbitrary quotients G of SL(2,Ẑ) is not known to be published

ideas.what: Reduction of the conjugacy conditions via characters ε_2 (mod 4) and ε_3 (mod 3) of μ. The ρ-condition is recast as conjugation by an element of the semidirect product G' = {1,τ}G lying in the ε_3(μ)-coset.
ideas.modern_name: Branch-cycle lemma for elliptic points of orders 4 and 6; twisting by the outer involution

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines a GT-type group B_{ρ,σ} attached to an arbitrary profinite quotient G of SL(2,Ẑ), with orbifold inertia conditions at the order-4 and order-6 points and the cusp, plus the τ-twist. He then gives a parametrisation by (α, β, ε_2(μ)) in G' × G × {±1}. This anticipates 'GT of a finite group / of PSL2Z-quotients' constructions (e.g. Guillot) and the genus-one GT literature, done here directly at the level of the modular group's quotients.
missed.quote: Pour qu'un (u,μ) ∈ Aut(G_{ρ,σ}) × Ẑ^* soit dans B_{ρ,σ}, il f.n.s. qu'il existe α ∈ G^{ε_3}, β ∈ G tels que on ait
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an explicit, finite-level description of Galois-type automorphisms of modular-curve fundamental groups. Comparing it with Guillot's GT(G) and with elliptic/modular GT variants could show whether Grothendieck's τ-coset normalisation gives a cleaner framework for finite-level invariants of modular dessins.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but largely routine reduction (branch-cycle conditions mod 4 and mod 3). The notable point is the framework: a GT-like group for arbitrary quotients of SL(2,Ẑ), including the τ-twist. That idea is close to, but somewhat earlier than, later work (Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Guillot) and is not explicitly in Grothendieck's published texts.

The 'pour pour ... conjugué[?]' passage should read: 'pour ε_3(μ)=1 u(ρ) est conjugué à ρ dans G, et pour ε_3(μ)=-1 il est conjugué à ρ^{-1} dans G, ou encore : à ρ par un élément de G' i.e. par un élément de la forme α, τα avec α ∈ G (puisque τ(ρ) = ^σ(ρ^{-1}) justement ...)'. 'τω' is a misreading of 'τα' / 'τ(ρ)'.
In the Proposition, the image has 'Aut(G_{ρ,σ}) × Ẑ^*', not 'Aut(G'_{ρ,σ} × Ẑ^*)'.
'Ceci vient de ce que σ' is a misreading. The line reads 'Comme ... de même on a' (introducing (9)).
The struck crossed-out block reads '(pour (u,μ) ∈ B_{ρ,σ}) des relations et il faut α ∈ G', β ∈ G'.
